newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Former W.Australia deputy premier convicted of perjury.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Former W.Australia deputy premier convicted of perjury.

text.p: Former West Australian Deputy Premier David Parker was remanded in custody on Wednesday after being convicted on five charges of willfully giving false evidence to the 1991 "WA INC" Royal Commission.
District court judge Michael Muller found Parker not guilty of a sixth charge and said he will sentence him on Friday.
The six charges related to royal commission evidence given by Parker regarding the sources of about A$24,000 in A$100 notes that he had in his possession in late 1986.
The Royal Commission into The Commercial Activities of Government and other Matters "(WA INC") was investing allegations that Parker had received a bribe from businessman Yosse Goldberg.
In his published reasons for judgement, Judge Muller said the crown had "unequivocally conceded there was no evidence the accused had acquired the money by improper means".

"(However), the accussed, when called upon to explain the source of his cash funds at the relevant time, is alleged to have consisently lied to the Royal Commission on a matter that was material to the enquiry being made by the Commission at that time," Judge Muller said.
Parker had told the Royal Commission the money came partly from his late wife Lorraine Arcus, and partly from savings from travel expenses.

During the seven day trial in the district court, the Crown alleged Arcus did not have sufficient assets to account for the money Parker claimed she gave him and that there was little scope for him to have saved large sums of money from his travel expenses.
In his reasons, Judge Muller found Arcus may have had the opportunity to give Parker some money but there were "a large number of circumstantial factors to suggest that she would not have done so".

He also said he was satisfied "the only reasonable inference consistant with all the facts I have found to be established is that the accused could not and did not accumulate" the money from his travel expenses.
